title: Underpromotion: See the Stalemate Before Taking
summary: A pawn promotion can offer the new queen for a forced capture that leaves its own king stalemated.

nodes.question: Black faces a queen and knight. How can the pawn save the draw?
nodes.explanation: Promote with check on c1. White’s only legal reply is Nxc1, after which the queen and pawns cover every Black king flight without checking it.

branches.title: Source defensive promotion and stalemate
commentary: Begin after White’s queen has captured the bishop on e5 and Black’s king has captured c4. All remaining a2/a3/f5 pawns stay on the board. The preceding queen promotion is context, not a certified forced sequence.
c1=Q+ promotes with a check along c1–b1–a1. White cannot move the king onto b1 or b2, and its a2 pawn occupies a2. Nxc1 is the only legal response.

Nxc1 removes the promoted queen and is stalemate. Black Kc4 is not in check: Qe5 covers b5/c5/d5/d4/c3/d3, a3 covers b4, and a2 covers b3. Black has no other piece or pawn to move. The exact position is drawn.

exercises.prompt: Why does capturing the promoted queen fail to win?
exercises.answer: After Nxc1 Black has only Kc4, with every flight covered but the king itself not checked. That is stalemate, regardless of White’s material.

exercises.prompt: Have all three underpromotions been proved here?
exercises.answer: No. This is the later defensive stalemate mechanism after the illustrated queen capture. The complete rook-underpromotion conversion still needs separate analysis.

startContext: Selected eight-piece defensive stalemate mechanism only, after White has promoted to a queen, Black has played Kxc4 and White has captured Be5: White Ka1/Qe5/Nb3/a2/a3/f5 against Kc4/c2, Black to move. The complete boards before and after these captures are visually reviewed; the selected root is their legally replayed intermediate, not an invented caption-only FEN. Black can promote with check on c1 and force Nxc1, which is actual stalemate. Independent analysis checks every Black root move, including all four promotions and Kd3; separate complete non-loss certificates prove this root exactly drawn. This is the same composition in two source clips, not two different games. The music-only clip supplies no chess narration. This scope does not prove all earlier promotion alternatives, claim that White had to choose Qxe5, or certify the complete earlier knight/bishop/rook-underpromotion plan and ten-piece rook conversion.
